items.rationale: Policy covers replacement of fixed technical installations damaged by insured perils (2.3.3, 2.4, 7.1.1(c)), but indemnity is limited to like-for-like replacement (7.1.10). Reference Case 38 shows kitchen AC units are not indemnified if not serving the insured building or if not a covered installation; however, here the description states both units were damaged by surge and needed replacing, so coverage applies. Reference Case 38 sets t below 20 for kitchen units, possibly 0, but that was due to proximity to the hob (excluded). Here, unless the kitchen unit is similarly excluded (e.g., too close to the hob), coverage is likely, but with caution.

Installation is indemnified only to the extent the principal item (the kitchen AC unit) is covered (7.1.11). If the kitchen unit is covered, so is its installation, but only for necessary, standard work (7.1.7, 7.1.10). Reference Case 38 sets installation for kitchen unit t below 10, possibly 0, due to exclusion; here, if the kitchen unit is covered, installation is too, but at a low rate.

A floor console is only indemnified if it is a like-for-like replacement of a damaged component (7.1.9, 7.1.10). Reference Case 38 shows t between 54 and 67 for a living-room unit's floor console, but kitchen units are not usually on a console. If the kitchen unit was previously on a console and it was damaged, indemnity applies; otherwise, if this is an upgrade or new addition, t = 0. Given lack of detail, moderate probability but at the lower end.

Ancillary charges (shipping) are only indemnified if the principal item is covered (7.1.11). Reference Case 38 sets t between 40 and 43 for freight shipping for a covered AC unit. If the kitchen unit is covered, so is shipping, at a similar rate.
